EDF is a fantastic Series, long running, and generally believed to be a strange but entertaining show. Let me tell you that 5 here isn't just entertaining, and just as fun as the previous 4.1 release, but the gameplay changes make vast improvements. now every class feels even more capable, even if some are arguably less powerful than before. Plus, the changes to the rewards system will cut down significantly on the farming for those seeking to collect everything.

   The campaign is as massive as ever. while the pace of the story may be slowed down compared to 4.1, the mechanics are just as swiftly introduced, and the large variety of enemies and their enhanced versions means there is very little drag if you're looking at just the play. The story though, many will quickly and reasonably be disregarded as silly and dumb. keep an ear out for the dialogue. while at will make you laugh, there are some amazing lines that can really drive in a dire and serious moment. You may be sweeping the battlefield, but thats one 1 location, when the entire world is under assault.

   The Weapons are truly what make EDF so glorious, and this game brings the most variety so far. as well as new types of support gear. Ranger is given not just tools to modify his sprinting, though you may be using those mostly, He also gets a selection of vehicles to try out. the motorcycles seem to be exclusive for him now. and are still a very entertaining nightmare to control. The Air Raider had a massive change, as now most of his tools aren't on the credits system to call, but instead reload naturally. however his vehicles and large explosive strikes are still on credits, to limit their power. Fancers had had a significant downgrade to their mobility due to the change in their dashes, but their support gear types vastly expand their base abilities. from a faster walk, to reducing the recoil on their massive cannons, so better control, or supplementing their limited dashes with more charges, or swifter cool downs. they're still the biggest and heaviest on field weapon. Wingdivers have had a real boost to their jetpack with the addition of support cores, expanding their fuel supply, recharge rates and even giving other bonuses depending on it's type. their weapons were given a new firing type as well. giving them a choice of magazine weapons, charge&Release bursts, drain-as-use, and even a few types that have a long reload, but no cost. No matter what class you pick, you should find something fun, or awesome, or just really reliable to use. Make sure to give everyone a try.

   The gameplay is a tried a true player-vs-enviroment type. you, your friends, and what Allied troops the EDF can give, trying your best to not only survive the massive horde of enemies, but smashing through to remove whatever is delivering more bugs to the field. you start off with meager variety, and hoping the Soldiers around you can clean up at least enough enemies to keep you alive as you collect those sweet colorful crates that drop all over the place. and soon you'll be leading the charge, or landing the big strikes to cleave apart the swarms of bugs. and right as everything gets nice and cozy, and you feel you can handle whatever size group of enemies, in comes a new type, and your momentum is halted, as you figure them out.

   The game is very replay friendly, the only real issue to that is how the Multiplayer, and local play mission lists have seperate progress. so you will find yourself forced to repeat missions when you first change over between modes. you don't have to worry though, as the host can bring you anywhere, as long as you have the difficulty unlocked. a Single complete of the last mission will unlock Hardest and Inferno difficulties for that mode. all your weapons do carry over between modes, so you won't have to worry about struggling to acquire those fun toys again when you want to show your friends. and this does mean you can farm for items and health on your own.

   Some of the shortcomings have still followed the series. the controls can be quiet peculiar, do yourself a favor at least take a look at them when you change class, Everything is rebindable, even on controller. You are free to make it all as comfortable as possible.

This will be broken up for newcomers to the series, and then a section for 4.1 veterans.

Those of you looking at an EDF game for the first time I want you to understand exactly what you're getting into; gratuitous explosions and the absolute quintessential "video game" experience you'll get these days. No where but EDF will you get giant insect genocide, going full Independence Day on aliens, and killing God. Four classes to choose from from the ever versatile Ranger who is as ground infantry as it gets plus a few tricks, Wing Diver who uses a jetpack to zip about and energy based weaponry, Air Raiders with their support based kits including team boosts, air strikes, missile strikes, and vehicle drops, and finally Fencer the power armor users and one man artillery units. Each of the four play in their own ways, and even within the classes individual load outs will differ your play from someone elses. "It's fun with friends" is a common statement these days but should never be the metric by which a game should be judged, EDF 5 will still keep you entertained on the chance you are flying solo.

For my 4.1 folks, this is essentially just *more* EDF, but when has that ever been a bad thing exactly? I do recommend picking it up on a sale or eventually price drop however. That said 5 offers a few updates to the formula that are pretty welcome additions including the following
-All classes have a dedicated "support/vehicle" slot now to increase their core in some in the form of Rangers body armors, upgraded power cores for Wing Divers, or frames for Fencer
-Weapons will upgrade over time with additional pick up. Find a favorite, keep doing missions and as you find more copies of it yours will grow in stats.
-Rangers can now sprint, increasing collection radius and generally zipping you from A to B a little faster and consistently than the classic side rolling
-Air Raiders got by far the nicest updates in the form of reload-based gunship strikes/cruise missiles/orbital strikes in addition to the battle credit call ins. The call in bombers now utilize a zoomed out aiming system instead of just blindly throwing a marking flare
-Wing Divers got a large change as well as *most* of their weapons now start at 0 capacity/magazine and are charged up instead. It's incredibly hit or miss sometimes but it's something you will get used to with a bit of play time. In terms of movement you now have a boost dash now which is just fantastic
-Fencers are now absolute speed and mobility demons if you run a boost/jump combo weapon load out

For the glory of the EDF
